paper_metadata.title: Temperature dependence of tensile behavior, deformation mechanisms and fracture in nitrogen-alloyed FeMnCrNiCo(N) Cantor alloys

evidence.quote: Among a family of the multi-principle-element alloys, a high-entropy Cantor alloy attracts much attention
Fracture mechanisms of the nitrogen-free and nitrogen-alloying FeMnCrNiCo HEAs

We studied the effect of nitrogen-alloying on the microstructure, temperature-dependent mechanical properties, strain hardening, deformation mechanisms and fracture micromechanisms of a FeMnNiCoCr high-entropy alloy under tensile loading in the temperature range (77–473)K.

evidence.quote: Four ingots of the multi-principal element alloys (MPEAs) were obtained by vacuum induction melting in pure Ar atmosphere using a periclase crucible. First, melting and degassing in a vacuum of inactive components (iron, nickel, cobalt) were performed. Then, chromium, manganese and MnN (for nitrogen introducing) were sequentially added into the melt through a dispenser. The molten metal was casted in an argon atmosphere into a flat mold.

The rectangular bars (10×10×25 mm3) were cut from the ingots and subjected to a homogenization and a solid-solution treatment with the following regime: annealing at a temperature of 1473 K for 2 h, multipass cold rolling up to 80% reduction, and annealing at 1473 K for 2 h with a subsequent water-quenching.
